clue.text: Really dislike finding a man to be wrong about one

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters wrap round the other piece
something gone wrong is out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a man has got one thing wrong and really can't stand it.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle the letters of 'a man to be' into ABOMNATE, then wrap that round I (one) to get ABOMINATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest, a strong verb for intense hatred.

clue.text: Non-drinker in a bar set to get drunk!

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The joke of a teetotaller being placed in a bar where everyone is getting drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer is someone who refrains from alcohol entirely, a teetotaller.

clue.text: Love good friends — they're jewels

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O
pals are good friends

explanation.surface: A sentimental saying that love and good friends are the real treasures of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones, so they are examples of jewels.

clue.text: Wise men fill in a journalist, it's thought

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: taken as written
the Magi are the Wise Men of the Nativity
ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: Sages briefing a reporter, or so it is believed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magi are the three Wise Men who visited the infant Jesus; 'fill' puts them inside the little word in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imagined is merely supposed or fancied, so it is thought rather than known.

clue.text: Making dope doubly popular is criminal!

parts.note: a dope is an ass, a fool, and doubly asks for it twice
something in fashion is in

explanation.surface: A warning that glamorising drugs is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs but means a fool; the exclamation mark plays up the moralising surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer of a prominent person, so a particular kind of criminal.

clue.text: Bearing a flower in spring

definitions.note: a description of the festival rather than a noun for it

parts.note: a compass bearing such as East, abbreviated E
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A plant bearing a flower in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a plant carrying a bloom, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival held each year in the spring months of March or April.

clue.text: Food for some Sherpa's table

indicators.note: only some of the following words are used, so a run of their letters is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Mountain guides in the Himalayas sitting down to a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian staple of dough shaped into noodles, an everyday kind of food.

clue.text: Having to recompense outside staff is a travesty

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to recompense is to pay
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: An employer complaining that having to compensate staff outside the firm is an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees being paid, but it is a stick, and 'outside' splits the payment word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation or mockery, which is what a parody also is.

clue.text: White-livered invertebrate

definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally having no backbone

explanation.walkthrough: 'White-livered' is an old word for cowardly, from the belief that a pale liver meant no courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a creature without a backbone and, figuratively, a weak cowardly person.

clue.text: The church lacking change, many will give such a coin

indicators.note: lacking means something is missing, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: Spare change dropped in a church collection plate adds up to a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CH from CHANGE to leave ANGE, then add L.
explanation.definitionFit: The angel was an old English gold coin stamped with the archangel Michael, so 'such a coin' names one.

clue.text: A deep-voiced vocalist in the main?

definitions.text: A deep-voiced vocalist in the main?

parts.note: surface reading: a singer with the lowest male voice
setter's reading: the main is the open ocean, so this is a fish living there whose name sounds like a low singer

explanation.surface: A low-voiced singer who mostly performs, on the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', but the main is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bass is a marine fish, and its name joins the ocean with the low male singing voice.

clue.text: Make a song about leaving when separating into classes

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
an ort is a scrap of food left over, a leaving

explanation.surface: Writing a song about saying goodbye while sorting things into groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' looks like departure, but leavings are leftovers, and ORT is an old word for a scrap left after a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorting means arranging items by kind or category, dividing them into groups.

clue.text: The musician's very very good on a ship

parts.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship
A1 means first-class, written with I for the figure 1

explanation.surface: A performer aboard a vessel is praised as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'very' twice on purpose: once in the definition and again inside 'very good', the A1 piece. 'On' places that piece after A and SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian tempo marking meaning 'very', as in allegro assai, used by musicians.

clue.text: Plant rush to excellent effect

parts.note: to rush is to speed
something done well is done to excellent effect

explanation.surface: Planting in a hurry and getting a great result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' suggests a reed, a plant, which makes 'Plant rush' tempt as one phrase; Plant is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small wild flower of the genus Veronica, usually with blue blooms.

clue.text: Modern erection — badly designed

indicators.note: something badly designed is put together wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A critic calls a new building an eyesore.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoteric is a learned word meaning recent or newfangled, from the Greek for newer.

clue.text: Before  the  finish  rebuilding proves to be uneconomical

indicators.note: rebuilding means putting together again in a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: six letters to rearrange
the finish is the end

explanation.surface: A building project that turns out, before completion, to be too costly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts the rearranged letters ahead of END.
explanation.definitionFit: To overspend is to pay out more than a budget allows, the opposite of being thrifty.

clue.text: Rows dividing the faithful

parts.note: surface reading: quarrels that split believers into factions
setter's reading: lines of church benches where the congregation sits in separate rows

explanation.surface: Doctrinal arguments that cause a split in a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as quarrels (rhyming with cows), but it means lines of seats (rhyming with toes).
explanation.definitionFit: Church benches stand in lines and separate the worshippers into groups of seated people.

clue.text: The only one in a suit wearing a vest

definitions.text: The only one in a suit

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest, the British word for an undershirt
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A lone man in a business suit with a vest underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing, matching the vest, but here it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a singleton is a hand holding just one card of a given suit.

clue.text: Remove the back seat

parts.note: surface reading: taking out the rear seat of a car
setter's reading: the seat strapped on a horse's back, which a rider takes off

explanation.surface: Taking out the rear bench of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsaddle a horse is to take off the leather riding seat fastened across its back.

clue.text: Leftists with acrimonious following get the bird

parts.note: reds are communists or socialists
a tart remark is sharp and bitter

explanation.surface: Bitter left-wing agitators are jeered off the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' is the idiom for being booed, but here the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail, so it is one particular bird.

clue.text: Deplored coarse sound

indicators.note: sound means we go by how a word is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: coarse means vulgar or rude

explanation.surface: Someone disapproved of a vulgar noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret or lament it, so rued means deplored.

clue.text: French article about a family issue making no sense

parts.note: un is French for a
re means concerning, about
taken as written
issue means offspring, and a son is one

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece about a family problem that is senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem, but it means children, as in 'died without issue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is the absence of rational thought, which amounts to no sense at all.

clue.text: Canadian mock savoury

parts.note: Can. is the abbreviation for Canadian
to ape is to mimic or mock

explanation.surface: An imitation savoury from Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' reads as an adjective for fake food, but it is a verb meaning imitate. A savoury is a small salty dish or snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small bite of bread or pastry with a topping, served as a savoury snack.

clue.text: Stick a short notice in this place

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
here means in this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to post a brief notice on this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' gives the clipped form of advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or be fixed to a surface, the intransitive verb stick.

clue.text: Gloomy forecaster — not given credit

parts.note: surface reading: a weather presenter predicting bad weather
setter's reading: the Trojan prophetess cursed so that her true prophecies were never believed

explanation.surface: A pessimistic weather forecaster who gets no recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit' suggests praise or money, but here it means belief.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Apollo cursed this Trojan seer so nobody trusted her prophecies; her name now means a doom-monger ignored.

clue.text: Move quickly  in water but slowly on land

definitions.text: Move quickly  in water but slowly on land

parts.note: setter's reading: the fastest swimming stroke
second reading: going along on hands and knees

explanation.walkthrough: One word covers both: a racing swimming stroke and a slow creep on all fours.
explanation.definitionFit: The front crawl is the quickest swimming stroke, while crawling on the ground is very slow progress.

clue.text: What the film is all about

definitions.text: What the film is all about

parts.words: What the film is all about
parts.note: surface reading: the plot or theme of a movie
setter's reading: the reel the strip of film is wound around

explanation.surface: Someone asking what a movie's story is.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is the reel or cylinder on which photographic film is wound, so the film wraps round it.

clue.text: Love game disaster in last of series

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so these letters end up scrambled

parts.note: taken as written: four letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tennis player loses a love game at the end of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the last of a sequence.

clue.text: Mean to state how old one is

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: Someone intends to reveal their age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb meaning intend, but it is the noun from arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the mean is the arithmetic average, the sum of values divided by their count.

clue.text: Brave holding Eastern holy man the closest

indicators.note: holding means one piece grips another inside it

parts.note: to brave something is to dare it
E is the abbreviation for Eastern
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: A courageous person sheltering an oriental guru close by.
explanation.walkthrough: DARE holds E to give DEARE, then ST is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearest describes the person you love most, the one closest to your heart.

clue.text: A physicist's place

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Oliver ..., British physicist and radio pioneer
second meaning: a small house, a lodging place

explanation.surface: The home or workplace of a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Lodge worked on radio waves; separately, a cabin or gatehouse is a dwelling place.

clue.text: Looks on exercise 2as a problem in a sense

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Someone regards physical exercise as troublesome, in a way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down-or-across charade means after: the exercise word follows the looks word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness or pain of the eyes, a complaint affecting sight, which is one of the senses.
